name: tutorial-interactive
description: Plays the Tutorial Pit the way a first-time player does: every step is driven by a real click on the control the tutorial card points at — speed button, toolbar, hire buttons, blast panel, event choices — and each beat waits for the tutorial's own rails to advance (waitForTutorialStep) before the next click, mirroring the retired playtest definition's click path (seismic survey at 23,23; the box cut dug down the west face before the drill grid; drill grid on the exact 20,20-30,30 rectangle; haul before deliver). Every tutorial-facing step is role-marked 'player' or 'setup' (issue #479): a player step's interaction may not fall back to a console command, so a step that cannot actually be clicked fails the scenario instead of passing on a typed shortcut.

steps.description: Setup: load Tutorial Pit — the level regenerates the terrain at its own size and re-frames the camera. #553: cash bumped from $80,000 to $250,000 -- drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action, so this file needs a driving_center/training/drill_rig it never used to, on top of the original manager/driver/hauler/warehouse shopping list.
Step time-speed: coach mark docked bottom-centre, speed button glowing, mine still visible
time-speed complete: real click on the speed button cycles 1x to 2x, card advances to Hire Surveyor
Player follows the glowing Crew button — the tutorial card must not swallow the click
hire-surveyor complete: Hire clicked in the crew panel, surveyor appears on site

expect.note: The tutorial is on rails: leaving for the world map mid-step is how a player loses it, so that button must be inert while the tutorial is up (mirrors tutorial.json's hire-surveyor beat).

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage: hiring already grants Rookie geology (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts, same for the UI hire button and this console command), so this only raises the level for tighter survey estimates. No role tag — there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building, which this scenario does not need. Command mode keeps running it unchanged; interaction mode keeps it as an unmarked (legacy) command step.

the hired surveyor can actually be sent to survey: opening the Survey panel alone must already show a usable Run button — a surveyor who cannot survey is not a surveyor. If Run is disabled here, hiring grants no geology qualification and no button in the game grants one (mirrors tutorial.json's own standalone beat).

survey complete: seismic (the method the card names), target picked inside the step's outlined region (18..28), dispatched, and the surveyor walks out and works it. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock for the walk — no scripted `tick` needed once a click starts it.
hire-driller complete: driller hired through the crew panel

#553: build-driving-center complete: driving_center built through the Build panel -- drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action (a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole), and hiring only grants the driller their 'blasting' qualification, never the driving.drill_rig licence a drill_rig needs. This step and the two after it (train-driller, buy-drill-rig-assign) close that gap, the same deadlock class #552 fixed for hauling.

#553: train-driller, click half: driving.drill_rig course booked at the driving_center just built. Training itself takes real ticks (TRAINING_BASE_TICKS, balance.ts) -- command mode has no implicit clock between steps (unlike interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep), so the wait is its own step right below, mirroring this file's existing tick-1/tick-6 wait-only beats.

#553: train-driller complete: the training course finishes and the driller (employee #2) is granted driving.drill_rig. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick since it has no implicit clock between steps.
buy-drill-rig-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 drill_rig bought and placed on the terrain surface

#553: buy-drill-rig-assign complete: Assign clicked, then the tutorial's own clock runs while the newly-licensed driller (employee #2) walks to the drill_rig and boards -- the drill-plan step right after this one can only ever land a hole once this actually completes.

box-cut complete: dig the starter cut down the west face of the drill pattern before the first shot, so the blasted rock has a free face and a void to fall into (real open pits pioneer this access cut first). waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock — no scripted `tick` needed.

expect.note: Open pits start with an access cut dug before the first shot: blasted rock swells and needs a void to fall into (mirrors tutorial.json's box-cut beat).

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — see the geology assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: drill-plan, click half: grid tool dragged over the exact 20,20-30,30 rectangle the card asks for (spacing 5 makes 3x3 holes), confirmed. #553: this only orders the 9 holes -- drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action, so holeCount stays 0 until the driller (equipped above) actually drives the drill_rig to each one. The wait is its own step right below.

#553: drill-plan complete: the driller drives the drill_rig to all 9 ordered holes and drills them (sandbox-measured: a single driller/drill_rig lands a 3x3 spacing:5 grid on tutorial_pit in ~300 ticks door-to-door). waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick since it has no implicit clock between steps.

Defensive: a `tick N` step silently completes fewer ticks than requested if a random event fires mid-wait, and every subsequent tick then refuses until the event is resolved. No-op when nothing is pending.

charge ordered: Charge All Holes clicked — the panel applies its own form defaults and hole rows turn amber/loading (#554: charging is real work now, so the click only queues the order; the wait step right after drains it and confirms the tutorial advances to sequence once every hole has actually landed).
#554: drain the charge order queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) — the tutorial only advances to the sequence stage once every hole has actually landed.
sequence complete: Auto Sequence clicked, delay labels appear on every hole
blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, crater and fragments appear, Blast Report closed; the scores card then auto-advances into the scripted consultant event

expect.note: Close dismisses BlastReportModal, which auto-opens with the real report right after DETONATE; scores card auto-advances, so tutorialStep is checked in the next beat (mirrors tutorial.json's own choice not to assert it here). holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount resetting to 0 is checkable in both modes and goes beyond what the DOM-only playtest reference could prove.

steps.description: event-fire-resolve complete: the consultant dialog is answered through its own buttons, outcome read, then dismissed
hire-manager complete: manager hired now that the event is resolved

contract-accept complete: Accept clicked on the offer this step's `command` names. #513/#581: elsewhere in this PR the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id]` rather than a bare `.bs-contract-accept` (which resolves to whichever offered card leads the DOM), so a scoped click can't silently accept a different contract than the command names. That scoping doesn't hold under the tutorial's own rails here, though: tutorialStages.ts's own 'contract-accept' stage declares its live target as the UNSCOPED `#bs-contract-panel .bs-contract-accept` (not a specific id), so a click scoped to one exact id is racing the offer pool's own refresh clock (REFRESH_INTERVAL, Contract.ts) on top of the tutorial rail's own gating -- under real render load this file (300+ extra ticks reaching this point) hit exactly that race, the id scoped here rotating out of the DOM between the wait and the click. Unscoped instead, matching the tutorial's own permitted target: this step's only assertion is which tutorial stage is reached next (`hire-driver`), not which contract identity was accepted, so there's no silent-divergence risk the way level1-win-efficient.json's own scoped case guards against -- `command`'s own id (20) still exercises command mode's real accept path independently.
hire-driver complete: driver hired through the crew panel

Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage — see the geology assign_skill step above; hiring already grants Rookie driving.truck, this only raises the level. Kept for command mode, which needs it for its own explicit `vehicle driver 1 4` to succeed identically.
vehicle-buy-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 hauler bought and placed on the terrain surface

vehicle-buy-assign complete: Assign clicked, then the tutorial's own clock runs while the driver walks to the vehicle and boards — the #478 deadlock path, exercised for real. #553: vehicle #2, not #1 -- the drill_rig bought earlier took vehicle slot #1 (destroyed by its own blast, but the id isn't reused).
build-storage complete: warehouse placed by clicking the step's outlined tile (6,6) in the Build panel picker

haul-debris complete (#552): automatic dispatch sends the hauler to a reachable fragment with no player click at all -- the retired Haul button is gone, so there is nothing left for this step to point at. The step teaches watching, not clicking: waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock for the haul exactly as before, just without a click triggering it.

expect.note: The old reported bug this beat guarded against (no UI control anywhere could trigger `vehicle haul`) no longer applies -- #552 retires the button and the whole manual flow, so there is nothing left to get stuck on. No increased check on storedMassKg here -- like hauling-gate.json (Finding #33), the exact delivered tonnage is position/timing-dependent, not the thing this beat proves.

steps.description: contract-deliver complete: Deliver clicked with the panel's own pre-filled remaining amount, finishing the contract accepted earlier; the finances card then auto-advances. Left unmarked: command mode's own `contract deliver` fails synchronously here ("Not enough stored material" -- command mode's automatic dispatch (#552) needs real ticks to actually drive/load/deliver, and the haul-debris step above only advances a single tick, so nothing is ever in storage there), while interaction mode's identical click genuinely succeeds because the tutorial's own waitForTutorialStep gate only advances once delivery truly completes -- activeContractCount would drop to 0 there but stay 1 in command mode, so it is not safely checkable across both modes (same class as Findings #21/#22/#31). #553: contract ID drifted from #1 to #20 (see the accept step's own note); amount lowered from 5000 to 200 to match contract #20's own 430kg cap.
set-policy complete: Apply pressed in the Operations panel (redesign P5 moved site policy out of Settings) — the form mirrors the policy in force, and applying it unchanged still counts

expect.note: Applies without touching a control first — the form mirrors the policy already in force, and it used to leave the step stuck while the panel said the policy had been updated (mirrors tutorial.json's own note).

steps.description: tick-advance complete: the tutorial's own clock runs — the whole point of this step — until tickCount has advanced more than 5, reaching the closing victory card. No click and no scripted `tick`: mirrors the retired playtest's own beat, which was `letTimePass` only.

expect.note: Either closing card is a correct outcome: victory hands off to the completion card as soon as the level's profit target is met, which is campaign economy rather than playability (mirrors tutorial.json's own note).

steps.description: victory complete: level ends, card shows Tutorial Complete. Forces the transition so the scenario ends deterministically rather than waiting out the profit-threshold win check; not a player action — `campaign` is on the reused setup allowlist.
Final: the congratulations card dismisses itself and the game is unpaused
